questions.question: How sharp is the main subject?

real_s1.explanation: Within its top classes, this unit responds most to a single, sharply focused main subject, especially one facing toward or away from the camera. It is weaker on blurry subjects and on cluttered scenes with no single main subject. It also prefers photos without a warm color tint and subjects that fill a moderate part of the frame. The sharpness and facing-the-camera effects are the most particular to it, since its similar units do not share them strongly.

real_s2.explanation: The unit prefers photos with a clear, sharply focused single main subject, especially one facing toward or away from the camera, such as a vehicle or animal seen head-on. It is less active on blurry subjects, on scenes without a single main subject, and on warm-tinted photos. Its preference for sharpness and for head-on subjects is stronger than that of its similar units. Its dislike of scenes with no main subject is partly shared with them.

real_s3.explanation: This unit responds most to sharp, well-defined single subjects, especially ones facing toward or away from the camera. It responds less to blurry subjects and to cluttered scenes with no single main subject. It also leans slightly toward photos without a warm color cast. Sharpness and the frontal/rear-facing orientation are what set it apart from its similar units; the general preference for having a single main subject is partly shared with them.

null_s1.explanation: This unit is most active on photos that lack a single main subject, such as cluttered scenes, multiple objects, or textured surfaces and patterns. It is less active when one isolated, well-framed object sits fully inside the frame, and especially when that subject is small or slightly blurry. Facing direction, lighting and color tint have only weak effects.

null_s2.explanation: This unit is most active on photos that have no single main subject, such as cluttered scenes, multiple objects, or textured or patterned surfaces (prayer rugs, tables, piles of things). It is least active on clear, isolated, fully framed single subjects, especially small or blurry ones. The 'no single main subject' contrasts are strong across several questions, and the similar units do not share them, so they are specific to this unit. Weaker secondary leanings are toward sharp subjects and a cool tint.

null_s3.explanation: The unit is most active on photos with no single main subject: cluttered, multi-object or textured scenes, such as patterned prayer rugs, piles of fruit or fungi, and arrays of parts, rather than one isolated, well-framed object. Every answer that indicates 'no single main subject' comes out higher than the alternatives across the framing, cut-off, position and sharpness questions. Similar units mostly do not share this, since their percentiles on these rows are well below 95. There is a weaker preference for sharp over slightly blurry subjects and for subjects that are partly cut off.
